objective: Review the repaired Verilator native option parser overlay patch build-only validation result, accept only compile/link compatibility evidence, and select the next parser-behavior definition gate without claiming native parser support or sidecar execution.

review_decision.weakest_point: The repaired overlay patch now builds verilator_bin, but the evidence is still build-only. It proves that the V3Options.h/V3Options.cpp patch shape is compile/link compatible against pinned Verilator v5.048; it does not prove that the built binary parses the new options correctly, rejects invalid values, hands fields to the sidecar, runs an RTL simulation, or supports arbitrary filelists.
accepted_because: the source run gate used the repaired overlay patch produced by the compile-fix implementation gate
descriptor JSON validation, git apply --check, and actual patch apply all exited zero before build
autoconf and configure both reached exit code 0
the build target was limited to verilator_bin and exited 0
VERILATOR_INSTALL was mechanically defaulted to a checkout-local generated install prefix under artifacts
the run gate kept parser behavior, sidecar runtime execution, timing, arbitrary RTL/filelist support, automatic allocation, upstream regression, and upstream landing as explicit non-claims

accepted_claim_scope.verilator_build_success_scope: verilator_bin build-only for the repaired repo-owned overlay patch against pinned Verilator v5.048 checkout

required_next_gate.name: define_verilator_native_option_parser_overlay_patch_parser_behavior_gate
must_decide: the smallest parser-behavior command set to run through the built Verilator binary or a freshly reproduced equivalent build
which positive option parse case is required before claiming native parser behavior
which invalid cases are required before claiming validation behavior
whether non-numeric count suffix behavior from std::atoi is accepted, rejected, or explicitly deferred
whether generated build artifacts from the source run gate may be reused locally or must be regenerated from the recorded source commands
must_not_claim: coverage-output equivalence for a native-parser flow

non_claims: not a landed upstream Verilator patch
not a runtime or ABI change
not GEM benchmark or comparison evidence
reports and artifacts are generated evidence, not source of truth
